name: degen_t08
hypothesis: The 55.8% degenerate-repetition rate of SFT v2 (vs base 0-shot 24.7%, base 3-shot 6.6%) is produced by greedy decoding, not by the model. READ: degeneracy at t=0.8 below base's 24.7% => the loop is a decoding artifact and every greedy code-500 number today is measuring the decoder; at or above 55.8% => the model itself is non-terminating and the cause is upstream in the SFT data or recipe. Accuracy at t=0.8 is a different estimator than greedy and is NOT comparable to the 2.2%.
finding: The repetition loop is a greedy-decoding artifact: sampling at t=0.8 cuts degeneracy by two thirds, below base 0-shot's 25.4%. It hid nothing -- accuracy stayed on the floor and in fact fell (greedy is the better pass@1 estimator for a weak model). So the format-side numbers (fence rate, degeneracy) are properties of the decoder and must be reported with their temperature; the capability-side number (accuracy at the floor) is decoder-independent and now rests on firmer ground, having been suspected of being a decoder artifact and checked.
decision: Report every generative format metric with its temperature; do not build a repetition penalty (it would suppress a symptom that carries no capability signal); do not change the SFT recipe or the SFT pack on this evidence. The 200M-has-no-measurable-code-generation conclusion stands.

name: degen_t08_base
hypothesis: Control arm for degen_t08, missing from the original design: base 0-shot code-500 was scored greedy (0/497, degeneracy 25.4%). If greedy also suppresses base accuracy, the 'no measurable code generation at 200M' conclusion rests partly on a decoder artifact. READ: base t=0.8 accuracy still 0/497 (or below 12.6%) => the capability conclusion is decoder-independent and stands. Above 12.6% => every base code number today measured the decoder and the conclusion is void.
finding: The control arm the original design was missing. Sampling halves degeneracy on the base model too and moves accuracy not at all -- it was already exactly zero and stays exactly zero. So the capability conclusion is decoder-independent: across two checkpoints and two temperatures, every code accuracy sits on the floor while the degeneracy rate moves by 13-39 points. Degeneracy and accuracy are separate channels and only the first responds to the decoder.
decision: '200M has no measurable code generation in this regime' is confirmed and no longer needs the decoder caveat. Report generative FORMAT metrics with their temperature; capability metrics do not need it.

Two differences are by design and neither is a defect: the parameter difference (+33,659,904, +16.3%) IS the intervention, and the tree difference between the two runs is outside the training path. Throughput: both arms hold 57K tok/s/gpu at steady state, so the +16.3% parameters cost no measured tokens/s here -- stated as tok/s and param count only, NOT as free compute: reported MFU rises 48% -> 55% purely because mfu = 6*n_params*tps/peak (train.py:2560) puts n_params in the numerator while 99.9% of the added params are a gather with no matmul. Wall 1321s -> 1250s.
finding:
THE TABLE IS FULLY TRAINED, WHICH KILLS THE PRE-REGISTERED WATCH RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. The row-norm reading (scripts/ve_row_norms.py, runs/ve_row_norms.json) reads 32832 of 32832 rows above the decay floor -- not a few frequent rows. The WATCH text assumed 'a small fraction' of rows get touched at 500 steps; that was wrong by construction: 0.26B tokens over 32832 rows is ~7900 hits per row on average. So the 'few frequent rows won' branch was never live, and with the A/B flat there is no win to attribute either way. Movement is also NOT concentrated: the top 1000 rows of 32832 hold 15.9% of total delta, top 100 hold 2.7%, top 10 hold 0.3%.
THE FLOOR HAD TO BE MEASURED, AND THE ESTIMATED ONE INVERTED THE ANSWER. Three premises died before this number was usable, all of them caught: (a) 'rows differing from init were trained' reads the whole vocab, because the table sits in the AdamW `embed` group (train.py:779) and an Embedding's gradient is DENSE, so decoupled decay steps every row whether a token reached it or not; (b) 'a norm cutoff separates them' fails too -- the model inits embeddings to std=0.02 (model.py:453 via self.apply(self._init) at :388), so an untouched row keeps norm 0.02*sqrt(1024) = 0.64, and I had earlier quoted 32 from torch's N(0,1) default, which is not this model's init; (c) the floor I first used was ESTIMATED at 10x the median row on the premise that most rows stay untouched, and that premise is the very thing being tested -- it put the floor ~900x too high and reported 274 of 32832 rows trained. The floor is now MEASURED: step the real optimizer through the real schedule on a row whose gradient is always zero, giving 0.0322 relative (analytic 0.0323 for embed_lr=0.1 at train.py:263 with embed_wd=0.001 at :265 -- note line 820's decay-to-zero is inside `if isinstance(opt, Muon)` and never reaches this group). Every row clears it by >=2.65x, so the verdict does not sit near the 1.5x admission line. The selftest now carries the fully-trained table as a regression and asserts the 10x-median floor still fails it.
THE GATE-AT-1.5 INIT WORKS, which is what makes the flat result interpretable rather than a null launch: the arms track each other from the first logged step (step 10: 6.801 vs 6.798; step 100: 4.121 vs 4.110), so the VE arm is not spending its budget discovering a table hidden behind a zero gate.
decision: NOT ADOPTED. +16.3% parameters for -0.0001 nat is the whole case against it, and no seeds will be spent widening the bar for a change that is not being adopted -- the same call as A/B (3). Asymmetric summary, on purpose: there is NO evidence VE helps at 200M/0.26B, and the one non-flat reading (minimal_pairs -1.08pt) points the wrong way while staying inside its own bar, so 'harmless' is also unproven. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE: the hypothesis was never separated from capacity -- no equal-parameter control arm ran -- so a flat result cannot distinguish 'the mechanism does nothing' from 'the mechanism helps and the +16.3% of parameters spent on a gather hurts by the same amount'. It also does not transfer up: value embeddings are a nanogpt-speedrun result at a different scale and token budget, and a table fully trained at 0.26B may behave differently once the vocab is seen far more or far less often. To revisit, the cheap next step is the equal-parameter control (spend the 33.7M on width or depth instead), not another VE seed.

name: ab_untie_head
cmd: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3,4,5,6 SKIP_BASE=1 ARM=untiehead STEPS=500 scripts/run_ab_speedrun.sh  # then ARM=untieheadlr, same lane
notes: base reused: ckpt_ab_shapelr_base.pt (world 4, 500 steps, mix_200m_4b, seed 42). Launcher gained untiehead/untieheadlr arms and SKIP_BASE at 8692549b.
hypothesis:
b0-17: is the LM head's lr the mechanism behind the uniform embedding growth? THREE ARMS, TWO DIFFERENCES, because one difference cannot separate the two candidate explanations -- this is the confound A/B (4) could not close and 1e's ruling fixes it here (2026-09-03):
  arm 1  base (REUSED ckpt_ab_shapelr_base.pt)  tied head, trains at embed_lr 0.1
  arm 2  --untie_head                            own head weights, STILL at embed_lr 0.1
  arm 3  --untie_head --head_lr 0.003464         own weights AND its own AdamW group
base->arm2 isolates CAPACITY (+33,619,968 params = +16.3%, 206,128,200 -> 239,748,168; the SAME magnitude as A/B (4)'s value_embed table, because both add one padded_vocab x d tensor). arm2->arm3 isolates the LR MECHANISM at IDENTICAL parameter count. WHY THE LR IS THE SUSPECT: train.py routes any parameter whose name contains tok or head into the embed group, so today's tied head necessarily trains at 0.1 -- 28.9x the nanochat reference head lr 0.004*(d/768)^-0.5 = 0.003464 at d1024 -- and b0-10 measured tok.weight growing 1.43x per 500 steps with 7.9% effective same-direction rate.
READING (pre-registered): domain_loss unweighted mean against 0.24 nat (ds.seed_variance_0p2b), minimal_pairs against 11.5pt (be.minimal_pairs_seed_variance), and tok.weight growth per 500 steps against b0-10's 1.43x. Verdict written as TWO differences, never one: a flat base->arm2 with a moving arm2->arm3 means the lr matters and the capacity does not; both flat means neither is readable at this scale and the +16.3% is unpaid-for; base->arm2 moving alone means this is a capacity result wearing an lr costume.
BASE IS REUSED, matched on the four things that decide comparability: world 4, 500 steps, mix_200m_4b, seed 42. Its cfg carries NO untie_head/head_lr field, which is the default (False, 0.0) -- absence here is not drift. Tokens/step therefore match, unlike the (3)/(2a) pair where world 5 vs world 4 made the same step a different token position and inverted the sign.
GUARD: scripts/test_untie_head.py, four checks each verified red on its own broken world. The one that matters most is that arms 2 and 3 are indistinguishable in every log except one lr field, so arm 3 collapsing into arm 2 errors nowhere and prints one number for two experiments; head lr is read by TENSOR IDENTITY, not group name, because a missing group returns None and would pass as a match. Also pinned: untying zeroes tok's vocab pad rows (while tied, one zero_() covered both tensors, so untied they would train in one arm only -- 1e caught this before the run), and the head stays fp8-excluded by name.

BASE IS REUSED, matched on the four things that decide comparability: world 4, 500 steps, mix_200m_4b, seed 42. Its cfg carries NO untie_head/head_lr field, which is the default (False, 0.0) -- absence here is not drift. Tokens/step therefore match, unlike the (3)/(2a) pair where world 5 vs world 4 made the same step a different token position and inverted the sign.
GUARD: scripts/test_untie_head.py, four checks each verified red on its own broken world. The one that matters most is that arms 2 and 3 are indistinguishable in every log except one lr field, so arm 3 collapsing into arm 2 errors nowhere and prints one number for two experiments; head lr is read by TENSOR IDENTITY, not group name, because a missing group returns None and would pass as a match. result: THREE ARMS, TWO DIFFERENCES, and both differences are 9/9 same-sign but under the 0.24 nat bar. domain_loss unweighted_mean: base 2.8480 -> arm2 (untied@embed 0.1, +33,619,968 params = +16.3%) 2.8962 -> arm3 (untied@own 0.003464, IDENTICAL param count to arm2) 2.9139. base->arm2 +0.0482 nat (20% of the bar), 9/9 domains worse, sd 0.0342, t +4.23. arm2->arm3 +0.0176 (7% of the bar), 9/9 worse, sd 0.0116, t +4.55. base->arm3 +0.0659 (27%), 9/9, t +5.38. finding: THE HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, NOT UNSUPPORTED, AND THE REFUTATION IS IN THE WEIGHTS NOT THE LOSS. 1e's mechanism was that the TIED head trains tok.weight at embed_lr 0.1 through a second gradient path, which would make tok's uniform growth (b0-10) an artifact of that path. Removing the path must then reduce the growth. It INCREASES it: tok row-norm median 16.9115 -> 18.3308 (arm2, x1.0839) -> 19.8036 (arm3, x1.1710), and the LOWER the head's lr the MORE tok grows. The 11 alignment-padding rows [32773,32784) settle it, because they are never an input id and never a target, so they are reachable ONLY through the head and their movement IS that path rather than a proxy: arm2 and arm3 both read EXACTLY 0.0000 there (path completely removed, not weakened), while arm2's HEAD pad rows read 7.1036 against the tied base's 6.6575 (the path itself got 1.067x STRONGER). Named path fully removed, not weakened, effect moved the other way. WHAT REPLACES IT IS A GUESS, labelled: a tied table receives input-path and head-path gradients that partially cancel, and untying removes the cancellation so the input path alone pushes tok further; no gradient signs were measured, so only 'the head path inflates tok' is excluded. ARM 3 DOES NOT MEASURE THE LR MECHANISM AT STEADY STATE: its head reaches row-norm median 1.5375 = 2.4x the 0.64 init, i.e. barely trained, because 500 steps at 28.9x lower lr is not enough. Arm 2's head DID converge -- 16.4952 against the tied table's 16.9115, within 2.4% -- so arm 2's +0.0482 is not an initialization debt, while arm 3's extra +0.0176 largely is. CAPACITY IS NOT FREE AND NOT PAID FOR: +16.3% params makes every one of nine domains worse.
decision: NOT ADOPTED, and untie_head stays default False. Three consequences. (1) b0-10's uniform embedding growth needs a different mechanism: the head-path explanation is excluded by measurement, and the cancellation guess is the next thing to test -- it needs gradient signs on the two paths, not another A/B. (2) A/B (4) and b0-17 agree ONLY on the negative, and I overstated this before checking it: both spend +33,619,968 params (+16.3%) on one padded_vocab x d table and NEITHER pays for itself, but they are NOT the same result. value_embed is genuine noise -- per-domain delta 3/9 positive, mean -0.0002 nat, t -0.05, i.e. indistinguishable from zero in both sign and magnitude. The untied head is CONSISTENTLY WORSE -- 9/9 positive, mean +0.0482, t +4.23. So the shared claim is narrow: at 200M/500 steps neither use of that parameter budget helps. Calling them 'two independent arms of the same shape' would have claimed a reproduced effect where one arm has no effect at all, and the aggregate 'flat-to-worse' phrasing hides exactly that difference. (3) The copy-init arm (untied head initialized FROM the embedding table) is now worth opening, and its purpose changed: not to control for the initialization confound (arm 2's head converged, so that confound is bounded) but as the only arm that can separate the tok reverse-growth from initialization cost at all. minimal_pairs should be dropped from 500-step A/B readings at 200M: 4.33pt of spread against an 11.5pt bar is not a measurement.
